title: STILL PRESENT (r1): Substitute SQL still duplicates the live-slot ON CONFLICT predicate — now 5 sites, incl. twice inside substitute_reference_call.sql
evidence: substitute_reference_call.sql:37 "  ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN ("; :51 "  AND rc.status NOT IN ("; :52-54 "'form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused', 'objected', 'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed', 'partial'"; insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql:28 "ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN ("; insert_reference_call_skipped.sql:24 same; supabase/migrations/20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql:140 "WHERE status NOT IN ('form_completed','unreachable','refused','objected','manual_recorded','failed','completed','partial');"
detail: The r1 note stands: the live-slot predicate is maintained in five places; the rework added a second in-file copy (the UNION ALL successor SELECT), so drift risk grew.
recommended_fix: Extract the terminal-status list into one shared SQL fragment (or a pinned cross-reference comment); keep the ON CONFLICT copy adjacent to the index definition it mirrors.

title: Single-slot refcheck_edit silently discards the first row's typed trio values when two correction forms are edited interleaved
evidence: model.gleam:376 "refcheck_edit: Option(RefcheckEdit),"; client.gleam:3457-3462 "let edit = case model.refcheck_edit { Some(e) if e.call_id == call_id -> e _ -> prefill_refcheck_edit(model, call_id, refcheck_edit_kind_for(model, call_id)) }"; client.gleam:3472 "#(Model(..model, refcheck_edit: Some(updated)), effect.none())"; reference_panel.gleam:609 "AwaitingCorrection -> view_correction_surface(call, app, slot, edit)"; reference_panel.gleam:997-1008 "_ -> #(effective_name_value(call), effective_email_value(call), effective_phone_value(call), False, None)"
detail: Awaiting-correction rows render their trio unconditionally (reference_panel.gleam:609) but the model holds one RefcheckEdit; typing in a second row replaces the first's in-progress edit and its trio silently reverts to the dead-snapshot prefill — a later save re-contacts the failed address.
recommended_fix: Make refcheck_edit a dict keyed by call_id, or disable unowned trios while an edit is open, so each row's typed values survive.

title: §8.3 correction body deviates from the spec-quoted copy (applicant name dropped, wording rewritten)
evidence: copy.gleam:844 "pub const refcheck_correction_body: String = \"Check with the applicant, update the details here, and we'll send the invitation again.\"" vs UX §7.4 "**We couldn't reach Colm at these details.** Check with Aisling, update them here, and we'll send the invitation again." and UX §8.3 "Check with Aisling, update them here, and we'll try again."
detail: Guard 9 pins §8.3 copy verbatim; the shipped body generalizes 'Aisling' to 'the applicant' and rewrites the tail ('them' to 'the details', 'try again' to 'send the invitation again') although app.first_name is available at the callsite.
recommended_fix: Ship the spec line with the applicant's name interpolated ('Check with {first_name}, update them here, and we'll send the invitation again.'), or get the deviation approved.
